---
title: "Modules and navigation"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

For apps with modules, several editors or more than one navigation path.
Start with [Get started](get-started.html) for a single form.

## The navigation guard

While there are unsaved changes, the guard stops every tab change: a click, the
arrow keys, and `updateTabsetPanel()` from the server. To move tabs from the
server while dirty, acknowledge a completed save, call `discard()` and wait
for restored inputs, or call `pause()` first. Use
`guard_nav = FALSE` to turn the guard off.

For a multi-step form, allow movement between steps and confirm at the real
exit points:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
tracker <- unsaved_track(c("name", "age"), guard_nav = FALSE)
# In the UI: unsaved_guard(actionButton("exit", "Exit form"))
observeEvent(input$exit, updateTabsetPanel(session, "pages", "home"))
```

`unsaved_guard()` guards exit buttons and links with `guard_clicks = TRUE`,
which is the default even when `guard_nav = FALSE`. Use `tracker$confirm()`
for server actions. Tagged tabs always follow `guard_nav`.

Each blocked change also sets the input `unsaved_nav_blocked`, so your app can
react to it. Inside a module this input uses the module's namespace.

## Guard buttons and links

For a click in the browser, `unsaved_guard()` adds `data-unsaved-guard`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
unsaved_guard(actionButton("delete", "Delete draft"))
unsaved_guard(tags$a(href = "/another-page", "Another page"))
```

You can also add the attribute yourself, including on a modal close button.
Dirty trackers with `guard_clicks = TRUE` block the click. Discard or a successful
save replays it once. Keep editing cancels it. Server confirmation works
independently of `guard_nav`.

## Editing inside a modal

Keep `guard_clicks = TRUE` and guard the explicit close button. This server
recipe tracks a text field created inside the modal:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
tracker <- unsaved_track("modal_name")
observeEvent(input$edit, {
  showModal(modalDialog(
    textInput("modal_name", "Name", "Ada"),
    easyClose = FALSE,
    footer = unsaved_guard(actionButton("close_editor", "Close"))
  ))
})
observeEvent(input$close_editor, removeModal())
```

With edits pending, Close asks before discarding them. Escape and backdrop
clicks are not guarded otherwise, so use `modalDialog(easyClose = FALSE)`.
The guard does not intercept a server call to `removeModal()`; confirm other
server actions before they remove the modal. Add `on_save` and your app's save
code if the dialog should also offer Save and continue.

## Modules

For a module-local count, use a custom output. The built-in badge shows the
page total. Each module can use this pattern:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
editor_ui <- function(id) {
  ns <- NS(id)
  tagList(textInput(ns("name"), "Name"), textOutput(ns("count")))
}
editor_server <- function(id) {
  moduleServer(id, function(input, output, session) {
    tracker <- unsaved_track("name")
    output$count <- renderText(paste(tracker$count(), "changed fields"))
    tracker
  })
}
```

Create the tracker inside `moduleServer()` with local input ids. Do not
prefix them with `session$ns()`. Save, discard and event inputs use that
module's namespace. For page totals and shared guards, see below.

## Use with rewind

`rewind` is an optional package for undo and redo:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
rewind::rewind_enable(inputs = "name")
tracker <- unsaved_track("name")
observeEvent(input$undo, rewind::rewind_undo())
observeEvent(input$redo, rewind::rewind_redo())
```

Undoing to saved values clears dirty state. Redo makes the form dirty again.
Discard is a normal edit, so rewind can undo it. For text, slow typing makes
several history steps; `updateOn = "blur"` gives one per edit. Ctrl+Z inside
a text box uses the browser's own undo, so use rewind's controls or API.

## Several trackers

Navigation guards cover the whole page. Each badge counts distinct changed
fields across all active trackers, including modules. Paused trackers do not
contribute. For a module count, use the custom output above.

A shared dialog uses the first involved tracker's text. Save and continue
appears only if every involved dirty tracker has `on_save`. Each tracker
saves on its own. One can succeed while another fails; nothing is rolled
back. Use one tracker and one save for fields that must save together.
If any involved tracker requires a reason, the shared dialog asks for one.
It passes that reason to each callback that requires it.
See [Saving](saving.html) for callback rules.

## Pause or stop tracking

`pause()` hides markers and badge counts and disables the guards.
The baseline stays in place. Queries still report real differences.
`resume()` restores the markers, counts and guards against that baseline.
Explicit `confirm()` still asks when a paused tracker is dirty.

`destroy()` stops tracking and removes the markers, counts and guards.
It cancels a pending confirmation and clears the saving flag, but does not
cancel save work. Repeated calls are safe. Commands do nothing after it.
Destruction runs on session end and on module destruction where Shiny
supports it.

See [Get started](get-started.html) for `confirm()` and record loading.
